skills.name: European science, technology and uneven change before the First World War

note.text: Between 1870 and 1914, industrial Europe saw wider use of steel, electricity, chemical production and faster communications. Rail and steam transport expanded from earlier foundations, while motor vehicles and early aviation developed. Germ theory and antiseptic practice changed medicine, though access and public health remained uneven. Expanding armies and naval competition linked technology to military rivalry. These changes had earlier roots and international connections; not every invention originated in Europe or within this period.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to connect selected innovations with medicine, transport and military competition without anachronism. Builds on: earlier industrialisation and international rivalry. Leads to: the social and global impact of industrial growth.

sections.heading: Explain the history
sections.text: Between {1870} and {1914}, industrial Europe saw wider use of steel, electricity, chemical production and faster communications. Rail and steam transport expanded from earlier foundations, while motor vehicles and early aviation developed. Germ theory and antiseptic practice changed medicine, though access and public health remained uneven. Expanding armies and naval competition linked technology to military rivalry. These changes had earlier roots and international connections; not every invention originated in Europe or within this period.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: A late industrial city could combine electric lighting with poor housing and unequal medical access. New transport could move goods and people faster without eliminating cost or exclusion. British parliamentary discussion in March {1914} compared dreadnought-type fleets, showing how industrial capacity entered naval rivalry. Antibiotics as widely used treatments belong to a later period, not a universal medical reality before {1914}.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Electricity and railways had no history before {1870}. Correction: Their roots predated the period of wider adoption.
Modern antibiotics were universally available across Europe before {1914}. Correction: That is an anachronistic claim about a later treatment era.
Faster transport eliminated every cost and inequality. Correction: Infrastructure and access remained uneven.
Industrial military expansion automatically guaranteed peace. Correction: Competition could intensify insecurity rather than remove it.
